static_traits.name: Gao Lei
static_traits.family_status: Living with spouse and two children
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive spouse with whom emotions and thoughts can be discussed; the marriage is somewhat affected by self-labeling
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Fairly cooperative, can describe events and feelings concretely, clear language, neutral tone

basic_info.main_problem: Often labeling oneself 'a terrible Father' over small mistakes, producing guilt and worthlessness.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent guilt and worthlessness affecting emotions and family interaction, hoping to ease these negative thoughts and become a better husband and Father.
growth_experiences: About a year ago Work demands and family responsibilities increased simultaneously, gradually intensifying the pressure of balancing Work and family; since then, whenever self-perceived mistakes occur in parenting and family matters, falling into intense guilt and Self-denial, further affecting marital quality, interactions with children, and Work performance.

core_beliefs: I am a failure/I have no value

special_situations.event: At a restaurant, discovers the reservation time is an hour late, family needs to wait, children become irritable
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If even simple family arrangements cannot be handled well, it proves I am a bad father and husband
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labels themselves negatively, blames themselves repeatedly, focusing attention on 'I ruined this evening'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a terrible father / I ruined this family outing

special_situations.event: Periods when increased Work demands make it impossible to give children enough attention
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If Work and family cannot be balanced simultaneously, it equals failure and will disappoint the family
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent self-criticism and confiding in the spouse, but not yet conducting systematic evidence testing and reevaluation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I disappointed my family, I am incompetent

special_situations.event: Small mistakes in parenting or housework (such as scheduling errors)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as it is not perfectly flawless, it means I am just a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labeling with 'terrible Father', falling into guilt and worthlessness
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I always mess up / I am just a failure

special_situations.event: Scenarios where family expresses understanding of mistakes and the outcome was not too bad
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even if others do not think it is serious, my feeling is the fact; I must take responsibility for the mistake to the end
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Clings to negative evaluations, ignores positive evidence and actual results
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Although they say it is nothing, I really messed things up

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and affirmed by family, to become a qualified and reliable father and husband
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and incompetence, worrying about disappointing the family and being seen as worthless
defense_goal: Maintains high standards through self-berating to avoid making mistakes again
Gains a sense of control and safety over mistakes through self-blame and labeling

object_relations.self_representation: A failure who disappoints the family/an incompetent Father
object_relations.object_representation: Understanding and supportive family (wife and children)
Family members hurt by one's own mistakes

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When in counseling reviewing 'small mistakes' or being invited to examine actual outcomes and evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Interprets small mistakes as total failure and believes she must bear full responsibility
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blaming statements, emphasizing own faults, ignoring others' understanding and positive outcomes; heavy tone, repeating expressions like 'It is all my fault'.

manifestations: Frequently self-labeling as 'a terrible Father', accompanied by significant worthlessness
Hard to enjoy activities with family, loses positive sense of meaning about her own role
Interactions with family becoming distant, irritable and Withdrawn under pressure and self-blame

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequently defines himself as a 'bad father' and 'failure'
Over-examining and Reflecting on small mistakes, ignoring positive real-world outcomes
Persisting in negative evaluations even when family shows understanding

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Setting rigid high standards for own role (e.g., not allowing small mistakes)
Treating 'must balance Work and family' as an absolute rule, Self-denial once not yet achieved

exception_events.target_problem: When small parenting-related mistakes occur (such as a restaurant reservation going wrong), the client usually labels oneself a 'bad father', falls into strong guilt, and it affects interactions with family members.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In the situation where the restaurant reservation went wrong this time, the wife expressed understanding, the child eventually calmed down, family interaction did not evolve into serious conflict, and the evening was not 'ruined' as the client catastrophically Anticipated.
exception_events.reason: Different support: the wife's understanding and the child's emotional Recovery reduced situational pressure; the real outcome was inconsistent with the initial catastrophic prediction, providing positive evidence for testing.

positive_force: Has a supportive spouse and family support
Willing to seek professional help and try new methods (e.g., recording and testing thoughts)
Can be aware of the thinking pattern of self-labeling and guilt when making mistakes
negative_force: Cognitive tendencies toward catastrophizing and overgeneralization
Personalized attribution and taking full responsibility (Personalization)
Imbalanced Work and family pressure, leading to Low mood and Relationship tension

target_behavior.behavior: Self-labeling ('I am a bad father/a failure') over small parenting-related mistakes and falling into significant guilt and worthlessness
antecedent: Small mistakes in parenting or family affairs (such as scheduling errors)
Increased Work stress, when feeling insufficient attention to children
Unexpected events or under-Anticipation occurrences in family outings and interaction scenes
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized high standards and a cognitive framework viewing mistakes as total failure (catastrophizing, overgeneralization, all-or-nothing), and personalizing external pressure as proof of own incompetence.
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of 'control' over mistakes through self-blame and negative labels, trying to prevent repeat mistakes and avoid being seen as incompetent (inner punishment/escaping loss of control).
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent guilt and Low mood, reducing enjoyment and interaction quality with family, Marriage and relationships damaged, Decline in work performance.
